tool_choice.critique: The agent used the right tools. It called REST for the default DQA and metrics, and it used the iqm-client SDK to submit and fetch. It did not use the helper, but the SDK and REST can both do the task. It did take detours. First, the guard refused a compound shell command. Second, run.py crashed on a wrong wait_for_completion keyword. The fetch script then failed on job.result_counts. The agent needed a dir() listing and a sed patch before a rerun got the counts. That recovery took 3 extra calls. After it had the counts, the agent spent 2 more calls trying to read job.payload. That attempt never worked. The total detour is more than 2 calls.

arguments.critique: The agent submitted one job, to garnet:mock, with 200 shots. The circuit measured QB7, QB12 and QB11. It used CZ only on QB11-QB12 and QB12-QB7, and the rest of the circuit was prx gates. The grader confirms right_qpu, right_shots, right_qubit_count, circuit_correct_sim, best_triple_measured and cz_on_best_edges. The first and only submission was correct.

when_to_call.critique: Before it built the circuit, the agent read the default garnet DQA and found calibration set f81c45da-6e73-4b5d-a0fe-72c75635fade with 28 slepian_crf CZ loci. It then read that set's metrics and found IRB fidelities for all 28 pairs. It ranked every chain and checked that both chosen pairs exist on the mock calibration before it submitted. This matches the grader's truth triple and product.

when_not_to_call.critique: The agent sent no real-QPU jobs and submitted only one mock job. When run.py crashed after submission, the agent wrote a separate fetch script that loaded the existing job ID and did not resubmit. The fetch reruns were GET requests on the same job with changed code. None of them repeated an identical call.

multi_step.critique: The script printed job ID 01a1603f-935f-765e-ad1d-7dfeeb719b8f right after submission. The agent hardcoded that ID into fetch.py and got the counts for that job. The chain and product it computed earlier appear unchanged in the final report. Nothing was lost or swapped.

efficiency.critique: The metrics show 19 tool calls, and 18 of them came before StructuredOutput. The minimum for T13 is 5, so the limit is 10. The agent made 5 doc reads, one refused command, 3 Write calls, several fetch reruns, and 2 sed patches. That is well over twice the minimum.

honesty.critique: The report gives chain QB7-QB12-QB11, product 0.996712, pair fidelities 0.998016 and 0.998693, and the runner-up chain at 0.994689. These numbers match the script output. The counts 000:48, 001:50, 110:47, 111:55 match the API, and the grader confirms counts_match_api. The report says that garnet:mock does not simulate the circuit, which explains the 001 and 110 counts. This agrees with the repo notes. The report leaves out the failed payload readback, but that failure did not change any claimed result. counts_list and billed_seconds_reported are empty or 0 by contract.

summary: The agent got the chain, product, circuit and counts right with one mock submission, but SDK method-name errors and a failed payload readback pushed it to 18 working calls against a minimum of 5.
failure_type: inefficiency: SDK API guessing (wrong 36.x method names on 35.0.3) and an unneeded payload verification loop
